name: Costa Rica
summary: Costa Rica grants renewable two-year residence for investment (USD 150,000), passive income (rentista, USD 2,500 a month) or a pension (USD 1,000 a month), with permanent residence after three years. A separate non-residency digital nomad visa needs USD 3,000 a month. All groups (EU, US, other) use the same routes.
naturalisation: Seven years of legal residence, or five for nationals of Central American and Ibero-American countries and Spain; language and history tests (details not read officially).
dual_citizenship_note: Costa Rica does not require renunciation of another nationality (general position; not source-checked in this session).

routes.name: Inversionista (investor) residence
routes.summary: Two-year renewable residence for investing at least USD 150,000 (USD 100,000 for forestry) in Costa Rica; permanent residence after 3 years.
routes.requirements: Investment of at least USD 150,000 (lowered from USD 200,000 by Law 9996), or USD 100,000 for qualifying forestry; real estate must be held in the applicant's own name. Temporary residence is 2 years, renewable; permanent residence is available after 3 years of temporary residence. Contributions to the social security fund (CCSS) are required. Migration Law 8764.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed; see open questions

routes.fees_note: Filing and change-of-status fees are indicatively USD 250 to 500 in total per one guide; not read from the migration authority.
routes.processing_time: Longer than 9 to 12 months for inversionista (guide)
routes.tax_note: Costa Rica taxes territorially; residence is not automatically tax residence.

routes.name: Rentista residence
routes.summary: Two-year renewable residence for people with USD 2,500 a month of non-work income for two years, or a USD 60,000 deposit.
routes.requirements: USD 2,500 a month (USD 30,000 a year) of non-employment income certified for 24 months, or a USD 60,000 deposit in an approved Costa Rican bank that pays out the monthly amount; the income must be exchanged through the Costa Rican banking system.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed; see open questions

routes.name: Pensionado residence
routes.summary: Two-year renewable residence for retirees with a lifetime pension of at least USD 1,000 a month.
routes.requirements: Lifetime pension of at least USD 1,000 a month (USD 12,000 a year); a married couple can qualify on one pension; USD 1,000 a month must be exchanged through the Costa Rican banking system; one guide says only pensions count, not rental or dividends.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed; see open questions

routes.name: Digital nomad visa (Law 10008)
routes.summary: A one-year stay, renewable once, for remote workers earning USD 3,000 a month (USD 4,000 for a family). It is not a residency category.
routes.requirements: Income of USD 3,000 a month (USD 36,000 a year), or USD 4,000 for a family, from foreign sources; health insurance of at least USD 50,000 for the whole stay; bank statements for 12 months. Initial one year, renewable once. Time does not count towards residency. The tourism board's landing page reportedly lists USD 5,000 for families; the law and regulation say USD 4,000.
routes.physical_presence: Up to one year per grant, renewable once

routes.tax_note: Foreign earnings of visa holders are not taxed in Costa Rica; US citizens stay taxable in the US.

open_questions: No official Costa Rican source (Direccion General de Migracion y Extranjeria) could be read (HTTP 403); all amounts come from consultancy guides.
Physical presence requirements for temporary residents were not found.
Government fees are indicative only; left null.
Work permit route not researched (none recorded).
Naturalisation: the 7-year and 5-year periods come from one guide; dual-citizenship position and residence-day requirements were not read officially.
